seoTitle: systemd Journal Viewer for journalctl -o json
metaDescription: Summarise journalctl JSON output by unit and priority, find repeated messages and filter entries. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Reads journalctl -o json lines and shows counts per unit and priority, top repeated messages and a table of entries.
why:
journalctl can export every field as JSON, which is complete but long. This tool shows which units are noisy and how bad their worst priority is.

Timestamps come from __REALTIME_TIMESTAMP in microseconds and are shown in UTC. Messages stored as byte arrays are decoded as UTF-8.
howTo: Run journalctl -o json --since "1 hour ago" > j.json.
Paste the output or choose the file.
Filter by unit, priority or text.
Read the summary or switch to the table.

faq.a: emerg, alert, crit, err, warning, notice, info, debug (0 to 7).
journald stores binary or non-UTF8 messages as byte arrays. They are decoded here.

faq.q: What if some lines do not match?
faq.a: They are skipped and the result says how many. Lines that are not JSON are counted.
No. Parsing happens in your browser and nothing is sent. Logs can hold IP addresses and tokens, so the page does not write them into the address bar.
